description:
Maintainer's architecture direction, 2026-08-04:

  'tampines will be an improvement of the turbine from tampines-steam-tables.
   The turbine from tampines-steam-tables should be based on TampinesSteamArray
   (HEM code) which will be the baseline that other solvers will be built on.'

TampinesSteamArray lives at crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:705 -- the homogeneous-equilibrium (HEM) array. It becomes the BASELINE that higher-fidelity solvers are measured against and built on (see the sibling bead for drift-flux / 6-eqn).

Turbine consequence: the turbine model in tampines-steam-tables today is ThreePhaseElectricGeneratorTurbine (steam_turbine_equations/generator.rs) -- a real, working lumped torque balance giving omega, EMF, current and power, but purely electromechanical: it has no steam path. tampines' turbine should improve on it by coupling that rotor to a TampinesSteamArray steam path rather than taking torque as a free input.

Note tampines::components::Turbine (components/turbine.rs:13) is currently inert -- inlet: HemSteamCv + adiabatic_efficiency: Ratio, and expand_to() returns NotYetImplemented. That is the shell this work fills in.

Remember the workspace convention (memory: arrays use (p,h) flash): TampinesSteamArray/OPCPFluidArray default to (p,h) flashing because it carries phase data; (T,p) single-phase flashes panic on two-phase.
title: tampines: TampinesSteamArray (HEM) as the baseline two-phase solver, and the turbine built on it

description:
`outram_mc_libs::rng::lcg::init_seed(id, offset, master_seed)` (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs:90) computes:

    let base = future_seed(DEFAULT_STRIDE, master_seed as u64);
    future_seed((id + offset) as u64, base)

i.e. future_seed(DEFAULT_STRIDE + id + offset, master). Consecutive ids therefore land ONE LCG step apart.

OpenMC's own init_seed (canonical source, /home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:60) is:

    return future_seed(static_cast<uint64_t>(id) * prn_stride, master_seed + offset);

i.e. id * STRIDE steps apart. The port drops the multiplication.

IMPACT: any caller using init_seed for per-particle / per-stream separation gets streams that are a one-draw shift of each other rather than independent — the exact opposite of the reproducible-parallel-MC guarantee the doc comment claims ('Each particle gets a unique starting seed by striding from the master seed'). Two particles' histories would be near-perfectly correlated. Needs checking against the actual transport call sites: if init_seed is used to seed particle streams, k-eff statistics may be affected.

FOUND BY: the raffles samplers port (op-vjw.2), which needs independent per-dimension streams for Latin hypercube sampling. raffles works around it by calling future_seed(stream * DEFAULT_STRIDE, master) directly with OpenMC's semantics; the workaround and the discrepancy are documented in crates/raffles/src/samplers.rs (stream_seed) and crates/raffles/CLAUDE.md.

SUGGESTED FIX: future_seed((id + offset) as u64 * DEFAULT_STRIDE, master_seed as u64), plus a regression test asserting that init_seed(k) and init_seed(k+1) are DEFAULT_STRIDE steps apart. Verify against the C++ before changing — the offset placement differs too (OpenMC adds offset to the master seed, this port adds it to the id).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
FIX IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-06 (uncommitted, awaiting maintainer review — AI output is untrusted draft per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md).

crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs now mirrors /home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:60-64:

    pub fn init_seed(id: i64, offset: i64, master_seed: i64) -> u64 {
        future_seed(
            (id as u64).wrapping_mul(DEFAULT_STRIDE),
            master_seed.wrapping_add(offset) as u64,
        )
    }

Both defects in this bead are fixed: id now MULTIPLIES the stride (streams 152917 draws apart, not 1), and offset is added to the MASTER SEED (independent run, not a shift within one). Signature kept per the maintainer's instruction; the master_seed parameter is documented as a deliberate deviation from OpenMC's global.

BLAST RADIUS (measured, not assumed): init_seed had ZERO library call sites. Its only users are 5 sites in examples/triso_stochastic_gpu.rs. All library transport code (physics::keff, pebble_beds::keff_delta, physics::transport_csg, gpu::batched_*) already calls future_seed(idx * STRIDE, base) directly with correct OpenMC semantics, so no k-eff or transport statistic was ever produced through the bug.

TESTS: 4 new regression tests in rng::lcg::tests, each verified to FAIL against the old implementation:
  - init_seed_consecutive_ids_are_one_full_stride_apart
  - init_seed_matches_openmc_golden_values (5 golden seeds computed by an independent Python implementation of the upstream recurrence)
  - init_seed_streams_do_not_overlap (old impl: 4095/4095 lag-1 exact matches — stream 1 WAS stream 0 shifted one draw)
  - init_seed_offset_selects_an_independent_run
Suite: 234 -> 238 passing, 0 failed, 0 pre-existing test moved.

RECORDED RESULTS: verification_and_validation/gpu_benchmarks/triso_stochastic_cls_gpu.csv was stale (produced 2026-07-21 through the bug). Re-run 2026-08-06 on an RTX A5000; CSV regenerated and the example's V&V doc block updated with the new measured values plus an explicit supersession note. CPU f64 reference moved 0.7013826 -> 0.7014103 (+0.0000277, 0.04 sigma) — the central value was barely biased; what was invalid was the quoted binomial sigma, since neighbouring histories were not independent samples.

SIBLING DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED HERE: rng::lcg::prn omits OpenMC's PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation -> filed as op-jis (P1). Larger blast radius (all recorded stats + WGSL shaders + raffles), needs its own planned change.
ALSO: 2 pre-existing doctest failures in geometry::surface unrelated to this -> op-keh (P2).

title: outram-mc-libs: init_seed derives streams 1 step apart, not 1 stride apart
